For those who do not know, sets have been a part of Voat for a while now, but today a new set was added to the website -- /s/GreatAwakening, which combines /v/GreatAwakening and /v/TheAwakening into one page that can be subscribed to and viewed. All posts from both subverses are combined in one feed for those who want to view content from both subverses.

Previous to now, the existing sets combined subverses with similar topics -- sports, news, images, music. As can be seen from the small number of subscribers, very few people knew these sets existed -- or if many did know, most did not care. This is understandable, as the existing sets were not that useful. Voat's front page resembles the Default and News sets most of the time, due to the disproportionate amount of content that is posted to /v/news, /v/politics, and the like.

But a custom set could have a great deal of use. As a migration aid, as one user pointed out, but also more generally as a means of preventing communities from being divided. Oldgoats might remember the old /v/AskVoat dramas, and the creation of /v/askvoat2 and /v/askgoat -- with custom sets, all these communities could be united. If someone ever feels the need to browse /v/askvoat, they could browse the set that unites all similar subverses.

Custom sets would also enable to unifying of similar content in any sense on Voat. Any uniting theme could bring subverses together into a single set that users can subscribe to or just view when interested in exploring that theme.

The only issue I see with the enabling of custom sets (and note: this hasn't happened yet. At this time Putt has simply added an additional set to the existing list; set creation remains disabled for users) would be awareness. Most people are so used to viewing either front pages or specific subverses, that most won't even think to make use of an in-between that shows posts from various similar subverses. We will see how effective Putt's stickies submission introducing this new set is at attracting users to make use of it, but I fear the numbers will be much lower than the total number of users of the two aforementioned subverses.
